name: dotnet-msix
Packages MSIX apps: creation, signing, Store submission, sideloading, auto-update, bundles, and CI/CD.

Assumptions: Windows App SDK 1.6+, Windows 10 build 19041+ for MSIX with Windows App SDK, build 1709+ for App Installer auto-update, .NET 8.0+.

Modern WinUI 3/Windows App SDK apps can package directly from `.csproj` with `WindowsPackageType`; WPF/WinForms use a Visual Studio Windows Application Packaging Project (`.wapproj`), which uses a specialized format, not `Microsoft.NET.Sdk`. Reference the app with:
`<ProjectReference Include="..\MyWpfApp\MyWpfApp.csproj" />`
Configure manifest identity, capabilities, and assets. See [skill:dotnet-winui] for WinUI setup/packaging comparison; [skill:dotnet-native-aot] for AOT; [skill:dotnet-gha-patterns] and [skill:dotnet-ado-patterns] for CI/CD; [skill:dotnet-nuget-authoring] for NuGet; [skill:dotnet-containers] for containers.

Build:
dotnet publish --configuration Release --runtime win-x64 \

All MSIX packages must be signed to install on Windows. The signing certificate's Subject must match the `Publisher` attribute in the package manifest.

$cert = New-SelfSignedCertificate `
-Subject "CN=My Company, O=My Company, L=Seattle, S=WA, C=US" `
-FriendlyName "MyApp Dev Signing" `
-CertStoreLocation "Cert:\CurrentUser\My" `
-TextExtension @("<REDACTED_IP>={text}<REDACTED_IP>.<REDACTED_IP>.3", `
"<REDACTED_IP>={text}")
$password = ConvertTo-SecureString -String "$env:CERT_PASSWORD" -Force -AsPlainText
Export-PfxCertificate -Cert $cert `
-FilePath "MyApp_DevSigning.pfx" `
$signtool = Get-ChildItem "C:\Program Files (x86)\Windows Kits\10\bin\*\x64\signtool.exe" |
Sort-Object { [version]($_.Directory.Parent.Name) } -Descending |
Select-Object -First 1 -ExpandProperty FullName
& $signtool sign /fd SHA256 /a /f "MyApp_DevSigning.pfx" `
/p "$env:CERT_PASSWORD" `
"AppPackages\MyApp_1.0.0.0_x64.msix"

For production distribution outside the Microsoft Store:
1. Obtain a code signing certificate from a trusted CA (DigiCert, Sectigo, GlobalSign)
2. Subject must match the `Publisher` in `Package.appxmanifest`
3. Timestamp the signature for long-term validity
& signtool.exe sign /fd SHA256 /sha1 "THUMBPRINT_HERE" `
/tr http://timestamp.digicert.com /td SHA256 `
"AppPackages\MyApp_1.0.0.0_x64.msix"
& signtool.exe sign /fd SHA256 /f "production-cert.pfx" `
/p "$env:CERT_PASSWORD" `
/tr http://timestamp.digicert.com /td SHA256 `
"AppPackages\MyApp_1.0.0.0_x64.msix"

Store apps are re-signed by Microsoft during ingestion; the development certificate is replaced with a Microsoft-issued certificate. No production signing certificate is needed for Store-only distribution. Development uses self-signed certificates; direct download needs a trusted CA; enterprise sideloading may use self-signed/internal CA.

Store: register at https://partner.microsoft.com/dashboard, reserve app name, build with Store association, submit `.msixupload` through Partner Center; Microsoft validates, signs, and publishes.

App Installer (`.appinstaller`) supports direct distribution and auto-update; host on web server, network share, or CDN. Configure update checks/prompts/background checks and downgrade behavior as needed.
ms-appinstaller:?source=https://mycompany.com/apps/MyApp.appinstaller

Enterprise deployment: Intune, SCCM/MECM, Group Policy, or PowerShell.
Add-AppxPackage -Path "\\fileserver\apps\MyApp_1.0.0.0_x64.msix"
Add-AppxProvisionedPackage -Online `
-PackagePath "MyApp_1.0.0.0_x64.msix" `

Differential updates download changed blocks automatically when the same `PackageName` and `Publisher` are used. See [references/detailed-examples.md](references/detailed-examples.md) for complete samples and advanced patterns.
